key_insight: SLiSDE replaces fully generic Neural SDEs with structured linear stochastic layers and gated stacking to make long-horizon simulation faster and training more stable for functional calibration tasks.
engineering_relevance: The framework offers a practical continuous-time model for computational science workflows where path-dependent objectives matter, while preserving parallel-in-time simulation and exact likelihood-ratio corrections when importance tilting is used.
method: Structured linear stochastic layers enable parallel-in-time simulation at each layer.
Gated in-flow stacking lets earlier layer paths modulate later latent dynamics to recover expressivity.
An optional Girsanov tilt acts as a learned importance sampler with exact correction for rare-path losses.
evidence_signal: Experiments on functional calibration benchmarks show the structured model outperforms fully neural SDE baselines while keeping stable importance weights.
watch_item: The added structure and optional change-of-measure machinery may require careful discretization and gate/tilt tuning to avoid bias or training instability in practice.
paper_title: Structured Neural SDEs for Functional Calibration
